root_causes.root_cause: RFC-029 D5c (post-Docling chart-page-detection heuristic) was marked complete in tasks-rfc029 but never implemented in code. No function for chart-page density detection or PictureItem synthesis exists anywhere in the codebase. Without D5c, Docling's Heron RT-DETRv2 layout model does not classify vector charts/bar-charts as PictureItem, so zero <!-- image --> markers are emitted and _recover_picture_results returns [] at converters.py:2225 (guard: _IMAGE_MARKER not in md). The entire picture enrichment pipeline never runs for chart-dominant PDF pages.
root_causes.code_path: converters.py:2225 -> _recover_picture_results entry guard (_IMAGE_MARKER in md) -> returns [] because Docling never emitted markers for chart pages
root_causes.suggested_fix: Implement D5c as designed in RFC-029: add a post-Docling heuristic that detects pages with very low text content relative to page area (<200 chars/page but known visual content from page dimensions/aspect ratio) and synthesizes PictureItem regions for them so they enter the existing picture-enrichment pipeline. This requires page rendering + text-density calculation + threshold tuning.

needs_doc_drilldown.reason: Symptom diverges from the shared RC1 pattern: this is a single-page German doc with a logo image (not a chart-dominant page), so D5c would not help. The regression (PASS->MARGINAL, 4082->2768 chars, missing image enrichment at node 3.5) likely combines judge re-scoring the same unenriched logo more strictly with content-processing char reductions from RFC-029 changes (NFKC normalization, fence/HR stripping). Needs per-doc investigation to separate judge-side vs pipeline-side causes of the 32% char drop.
